atoms.reason: Tri-source consensus. Strong isolation principle: a top-and-tail-delimited section with dedicated function prefixes and zero calls into worktree/merge/cleanup machinery cleanly prevents read-only audit jobs from ever triggering destructive worktree operations. Test is statically verifiable via grep. Low cost, high reversibility. Housing it inside lib/parallel.ps1 (vs a separate file) is justified by shared use of Get-ParallelJobsDir.

Consensus. A script-scoped registry keyed by root PID with cached Process handle and pidTicks is the correct backbone; pidTicks defends against PID reuse and the cached handle supports the atom-03 liveness check. Minor: 'synchronized' hashtable is unnecessary since Start-Process spawns external OS processes, not in-runspace threads — but the 'e.g.' phrasing leaves it optional, so no penalty. Slightly lower simplicity for the multi-field record.

Consensus and canonically correct PowerShell. Caching the Process object from Start-Process -PassThru and reading .HasExited avoids both the PID-reuse race and the throw-on-missing behavior of Get-Process -Id. Since the session owns these processes, .HasExited is reliable (no access-denied edge case). Highest-confidence atom of the set.

Consensus. Four per-job files (in/out/err/result) under Get-ParallelJobsDir with a distinct roaudit_<guid> prefix matches the existing parallel-jobs convention and the prefix prevents collisions with worker jobs. Consistent design: only three are redirect targets (stdin/stdout/stderr distinct, avoiding the same-file redirect error) while 'result' is job-written. Necessary plumbing of moderate impact.

Single-source (A). The intent — never count dead processes as active — is correct, but destructive 'pruning' (removal) is the wrong mechanism: it mutates state inside a Get- (read) verb, discards the metadata/result-file pointers needed afterward, and breaks atom-06's 'total' (launched) count and atom-08's proc=$null records. Modify to: compute the active count by filtering on cached .HasExited and MARK completed entries inactive rather than removing them; move any actual cleanup to a separate maintenance function.

Single-source (B) but sound API design. Returning a structured @{active; total; activePids} object is more extensible and self-documenting than a bare integer, and it composes with atom-07's peak-sampling (reads .active). Note the dependency this exposes: a meaningful 'total' requires NOT removing completed entries, which reinforces the atom-05 modification. Trivial to implement, fully reversible.

Consensus and well-constructed. PEAK-tracking the active count across repeated samples is the right way to avoid flakiness from sampling as jobs finish; the 6-8s sleep gives ample headroom for the assert peak>=3. Adding Parser::ParseFile syntax checks on both lib/parallel.ps1 and the test itself catches parse regressions cheaply. Works whether status returns an int or the atom-06 object.

Single-source (B) but a clear robustness win: wrapping each Start-Process in try/catch and recording failed spawns as proc=$null stops one bad job from aborting the whole pool launch, and the inactive record integrates with the registry and active-count filter. Caveat (covered, not penalized): not every failure throws — some commands spawn and immediately exit — but the cached-.HasExited liveness check from atom-03 catches that path, so the two atoms together are complete.
